details: Bitcoin (BTC) has extended its losses this week, trading below $82,500 on Friday and dipping to just above $80,000 after earlier US inflation reports. The cryptocurrency's decline aligns with a broader selloff in US tech stocks, reflecting a risk-off sentiment in the markets. Institutional demand for Bitcoin spot Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) has also weakened, with a two-week streak of net outflows totaling $146.19 million through Thursday. Investors are now closely watching the Federal Reserve's late-October decision for further market direction.
title: Bitcoin Dips Amid US Inflation Concerns and Tech Selloff

details: Crude oil prices surged above $100 a barrel on Friday, marking an over 11% increase this week due to tightening supply and robust fuel demand, exacerbated by geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. This rise contributes to accelerating consumer and producer inflation, clouding the outlook for interest rates. While Federal Reserve officials have not explicitly signaled an October rate hike, hotter-than-expected inflation data has led traders to scale back expectations for a pause, with markets now split on the likelihood of another 25 basis point hike at the upcoming Fed meeting.
title: Rising Oil Prices Fuel Inflation Fears, Impacting Fed Rate Hike Outlook

details: Circle Internet Group is expanding the availability of its USDC stablecoin into 40 new emerging markets across Asia, Latin America, and the Middle East. This strategic move aims to directly compete with traditional banks for cross-border payment flows, leveraging the efficiency and lower costs associated with stablecoin transactions. This expansion could significantly increase USDC adoption and utility in regions with high demand for accessible and efficient financial services.
title: Circle Expands USDC to 40 New Emerging Markets

details: MSCI, a leading provider of investment decision support tools, has adopted new eligibility rules that could put several crypto-focused companies, including Strategy and Metaplanet, at risk of exclusion from its indexes. This development highlights the growing scrutiny and evolving regulatory landscape surrounding cryptocurrency-related entities within traditional financial markets, potentially impacting institutional investment flows into such companies.
title: MSCI Considers New Rules, Posing Risk for Crypto-Focused Firms
